about: One row per public claim: wording, locations, evidence, exclusions and status. Wording rules per topic live in _claims.json; registry_ids point at them. Evidence pointers are repo-relative.

rows.wording: Inspect, visualize and intervene on any operation in any neural network
rows.models: tests/classics_corpus sample; Menagerie campaign outside this repo
rows.evidence_note: The tagline's scope is the backends TorchLens ships: PyTorch eager is the stable capture path and JAX, TensorFlow, MLX, PaddlePaddle and tinygrad are previews; replay validation over the Model Menagerie is the breadth evidence.
rows.exclusions: TorchScript, torch.export, CUDA graph replay, GPTQ/AWQ packed weights, sharded FSDP/DTensor topologies (see the limitations catalog).

rows.wording: logs the result of every operation it executes, not just module outputs
rows.evidence_note: Operation-level capture within supported execution boundaries; fused kernels and opaque extensions are one op each, and backward capture is torch-only.
rows.exclusions: Fused kernels' internal tensors; opaque C++ extensions; non-torch backends record derived leaf-level gradients, not backward graphs.

rows.wording: Every tool above is designed to work on [any PyTorch model](#model-menagerie), including ones with loops, conditional branches, and other dynamic behavior
rows.models: classics corpus recurrent and dynamic entries
rows.evidence_note: Dynamic control flow and recurrence are captured as executed (multi-pass ops); the classics corpus includes recurrent models.
rows.exclusions: Same as readme-any-pytorch-model.

rows.wording: of over 6,600 networks, spanning over eight decades of neural network history
rows.evidence_note: JMT's current Model Menagerie count, recorded 2026-11-05 (he ruled "over 6600" when the site showed 6,601; the Menagerie is its own project; the count is not reproducible from this repo).
rows.exclusions: Menagerie entries are not all executed checks; the verified subset is readme-menagerie-replay-carriers.

rows.wording: with 800+ metadata attributes in all
rows.evidence_note: The glossary lists the public attributes of every record type; no committed count of them is on file. The README no longer links the glossary from this sentence.
rows.exclusions: The figure counts attributes across all record types (operation, module, parameter, buffer, grad_fn node, trace), not per operation.

rows.wording: TorchLens runs on Python 3.10 to 3.13 with PyTorch 2.1 or later
rows.evidence_note: Floor legs in the nightly workflow pin the exact floor pair per interpreter.
rows.exclusions: Per-interpreter floors are higher: PyTorch 2.2+ on Python 3.12 and 2.6+ on 3.13 (no older torch wheels exist there).

rows.wording: A trace can also be indexed by a module's address
rows.models: test models in the indexing suites
rows.evidence_note: Lookup by operation name, name plus call number, module address and selector resolves to the same records.
rows.exclusions: Ambiguous keys refuse with AmbiguousOpLookupError (for example a module with two output ops).

rows.wording: Every operation, module, parameter, buffer, and grad_fn node gets its own data structure, as does the trace itself
rows.evidence_note: Per-op metadata fields are covered by the metadata tests.
rows.exclusions: FLOPs are formula-exact only for ops with a known rule; unknown ops are disclosed.

rows.wording: covering everything from each operation's output shape and FLOPs to the line of code that ran it
it shows every operation the network performs, in the same notation for every architecture
rows.evidence_note: Rendering covers captured graphs; very large graphs fall back to layout limits.
rows.exclusions: Models that cannot be captured cannot be drawn.

rows.wording: Each model is checked with tl.validate, which re-executes every saved operation and confirms that the results match the model's own output. More than 6,300 models have been verified in this way so far
rows.evidence_note: JMT's current count of Menagerie models passing tl.validate, recorded 2026-11-04; the Menagerie verification ledger is not in this repo, so the number is not reproducible from the tree. tests/test_validation.py covers the replay check itself.
rows.exclusions: Replay success is not by itself proof that every operation was seen; fused and opaque boundaries stay outside the check.

rows.wording: it also has backends for JAX, MLX, TensorFlow, PaddlePaddle and tinygrad
rows.evidence_note: docs/backends.md#what-works-on-each-framework is the linked feature comparison; every non-PyTorch backend is a preview.
rows.exclusions: Preview backends do not cover the full PyTorch feature set; see the capability matrix.
rows.say_today: Stable PyTorch and five named previews

rows.wording: fastlog_halt_25 is 0.84x raw forward on ResNet-18 (CPU) and 0.83x on
rows.evidence_note: Same measurement as readme-halt-faster-than-raw.
rows.exclusions: Only the early-halt case.

rows.wording: Capture every activation and gradient of any PyTorch model
rows.evidence_note: Same claim as readme-every-activation-and-gradient; set in repository settings, not in a file.
rows.exclusions: As readme-every-activation-and-gradient.

rows.wording: about 1x a plain forward hook
rows.evidence_note: Bound live edits measured at 1.0 to 1.2x a plain hook; refresh on the release before quoting.
rows.exclusions: Capture-free: no activations recorded.
rows.say_today: Bound live edits at hook speed
rows.before_strengthening: Refreshed matched measurements before quoting older ratios

rows.wording: Architecture-general design, diverse real examples, Menagerie with hedged count
rows.evidence_note: The classics corpus runs capture, replay and invariants on a coverage-chosen sample; the Menagerie count is hedged.
rows.exclusions: Structure-only entries are not executed checks.
rows.say_today: Architecture-general design, diverse real examples, Menagerie with hedged count
rows.before_strengthening: Audited, deduplicated counts by family, backend and check

rows.wording: Operation-level capture within supported execution boundaries
rows.evidence_note: Capture is per torch operation; the limitations catalog names the boundaries.
rows.exclusions: Fused and opaque ops are one op each.
rows.say_today: Operation-level capture within supported execution boundaries
rows.before_strengthening: Coverage tests plus fused and opaque op disclosures

rows.wording: Replay checks with explicit pass, unavailable and refused cases
rows.evidence_note: Forward replay validation and metadata invariants; unavailable and refused outcomes are typed.
rows.exclusions: Release-matched tamper controls are not on file.
rows.say_today: Replay checks with explicit pass, unavailable and refused cases

rows.wording: Stable PyTorch and five named previews
rows.evidence_note: JAX, MLX, tinygrad, Paddle and TensorFlow are previews with a capability table.
rows.exclusions: Per-backend, per-feature evidence is not complete.
rows.say_today: Stable PyTorch and five named previews

rows.wording: Bound live edits at hook speed
rows.evidence_note: Bound live edits measured at 1.0 to 1.2x a plain hook.
rows.exclusions: Full trace is far slower than a hook; older ratios are configuration-specific.
rows.say_today: Bound live edits at hook speed
rows.before_strengthening: Refreshed matched measurements before quoting older ratios

rows.wording: TorchLens helps coding agents implement interpretability methods
rows.evidence_note: A small docs-use study exists; the agent benchmark (pilot and confirmation) has not run.
rows.exclusions: No agent productivity claim anywhere until the benchmark numbers exist.

rows.wording: IOI circuit by EAP-IG at head ROC AUC 0.926 on GPT-2 small
rows.evidence_note: Measured on the development branch: head ROC AUC 0.9263 against the 26 Wang circuit heads, 1000 MIB IOI train rows, EAP-IG m=5. Not yet rerun on a release.
rows.exclusions: Edge recall at k=182 was 0.3956.

rows.wording: Attribution graph matches circuit-tracer on Gemma-2 2B within 8.6e-7 of the largest adjacency entry
rows.evidence_note: Measured on the development branch: largest adjacency difference 8.64e-7 of the largest oracle entry, relative Frobenius 1.10e-6, CPU float32, Dallas prompt, 9,170 features. A 1.05e-6 figure quoted elsewhere is the spread between two circuit-tracer environments, not the TorchLens agreement.
rows.exclusions: One prompt; CPU float32.

rows.wording: TorchLens activations scored on Brain-Score benchmarks end to end
rows.evidence_note: Measured 2026-10-14: MajajHong2015public.IT-pls 0.4408, Geirhos2021colour-top1 0.9547; seam parity max abs diff 0.0 against Brain-Score's PytorchWrapper on 24 stimuli.
rows.exclusions: Brain-Score is a destination: never 'runs Brain-Score' or RSA parity wording (U28.4).

rows.wording: new frontier models arriving faster than we can study the current ones
rows.evidence_note: Framing about the pace of the field, not a claim about TorchLens; the 'faster' coverage pattern matches it.
rows.exclusions: Not a TorchLens speed claim.

rows.wording: PyTorch has long lacked a built-in way to extract every intermediate activation from arbitrary networks
rows.evidence_note: Sourced to the torchvision feature_extraction docstring linked in the README (lines 391-405 at e334535a), which says extraction can take some massaging.
rows.exclusions: torchvision's FX-based create_feature_extractor exists; the claim is that it is not general across arbitrary networks.

rows.wording: Pass it any PyTorch model and its input exactly as they are, with no hooks, wrappers or changes to your code
rows.evidence_note: tl.trace takes the unmodified model and input; the classics corpus exercises that across architecture families.
rows.exclusions: torch.compile, TorchScript and torch.export artifacts are refused (log the eager module); concurrent captures across threads or processes are unsupported.

rows.wording: read the gradient at any operation, or at the grad_fn nodes PyTorch runs between operations
rows.evidence_note: Gradients are recorded per operation output and per grad_fn call when a backward pass runs.
rows.exclusions: Fused kernels expose no hidden internal gradients; torch.func transforms are boundary nodes.

rows.wording: patch in activations from another run (20+ built-in edits)
rows.evidence_note: Count of built-in edit helpers in the tl namespace; no committed census of them is on file.
rows.exclusions: Counts helpers, not combinations.

rows.wording: compute metrics across them at any operation, find where they diverge most
rows.models: any set of traces of one model
rows.evidence_note: Bundle metrics and divergence ranking over aligned operations.
rows.exclusions: Traces must align operation by operation; unaligned operations are reported, not compared.

rows.wording: a built-in validation function (tl.validate) can replay the forward pass to confirm that everything it saved matches the real model
rows.evidence_note: Replay plus metadata invariants per verified capture; replay success is not by itself proof that every operation was seen.
rows.exclusions: Fused and opaque boundaries; captures where validation is unavailable or refused.

rows.wording: at any operation you select
rows.models: eager PyTorch models with the captum extra
rows.evidence_note: Covers both README places (the Related tools paragraph and the Captum bullet): Captum attribution and SAELens export run at a selected operation, not only at module boundaries.
rows.exclusions: Needs the optional captum or saelens extra.

rows.wording: Any set of units you can describe by their kind, location and causal links to other units can be picked out with a single selector
rows.evidence_note: The linked page proves absolute completeness on one capture and relative completeness for a declared query language of attribute predicates, set operations and dataflow reachability (with two stated caveats); its worked examples run in tests/test_selection_completeness_examples.py.
rows.exclusions: Relative completeness holds for the declared query language, with the two caveats the page spells out; completeness is about where, not how much one site influences another.

rows.wording: Faster options reuse that graph or skip it
rows.models: LSTM tagger, ResNet-18 and GPT-2 small in the capture benchmarks
rows.evidence_note: trace.run, tl.record and tl.extract each measured below a first full trace on the same workload; tl.extract takes one plain forward with hooks when every requested module returns one tensor (1.10x a plain forward on ResNet-18 CPU, 8 Nov 2026).
rows.exclusions: A module that returns a tuple or dict (the LSTM tagger) makes tl.extract fall back to a full capture; trace.run falls back to a full capture when the call structure changes.
